title: U.S. House, District 14
what_it_does: Represents Florida's 14th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives; votes on federal laws and spending.
verified_ballot_note: WUSF, WTSP and AP (Aug 18, 2026) report Mike Beltran won the eight-candidate Republican primary and faces incumbent Kathy Castor (D), who advanced without appearing on the primary ballot (https://www.wusf.org/politics-issues/2026-08-18/hillsborough-primary-results-2026-mike-beltran-wins-republican-nomination-florida-congressional-district-14 ; https://www.10tv.com/article/syndication/associatedpress/mike-beltran-wins-republican-nomination-for-us-house-in-floridas-14th-congressional-district/616-2e360727-dc08-48af-82f9-ad35faa3f9a4 ; https://thehill.com/homenews/6033995-beltran-castor-florida-house-race/). Under the 2026 map the district lies entirely within Hillsborough County (eastern and southern Hillsborough: Brandon, Riverview, Plant City, Valrico, Sun City Center, Apollo Beach, Wimauma). NPA/write-in candidates not confirmed. Florida's Legislature passed a new congressional map in the April 2026 special session (Senate vote 21-17 on April 29, 2026) and the Florida Supreme Court on June 10, 2026 declined (6-1) to block it, so the new district lines apply to the Nov. 3, 2026 election; litigation on the merits continues. (https://floridaphoenix.com/2026/04/29/florida-legislature-passes-desantis-congressional-redistricting-map/; https://mynews13.com/fl/orlando/news/2026/06/10/florida-supreme-court-clears-way-for-new-redistricting-map-in-2026; https://www.wusf.org/politics-issues/2026-06-11/florida-supreme-court-rejects-challenge-new-redistricting-map) County list reflects pre-2026 district boundaries unless a 2026 source is cited; boundaries changed under the April 2026 map and the exact new county composition was not confirmed in searches run for this guide.

candidates.name: Kathy Castor
candidates.background: Kathy Castor, an attorney and former Hillsborough County commissioner, has represented the Tampa-based 14th District since 2007. She chaired the House Select Committee on the Climate Crisis (2019-2023) and sits on the Energy and Commerce Committee. She advanced to the 2026 general election without appearing on the Democratic primary ballot (Ballotpedia had listed Juan Arauz as a filer). The April 2026 map removed the district's cross-bay portion, leaving it entirely within eastern and southern Hillsborough County.

candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.background: Mike Beltran, an attorney from Lithia, served in the Florida House of Representatives from 2018 to 2024, representing a southeastern Hillsborough County district. He entered the CD 14 race in May 2026 after redistricting and won the eight-candidate Aug. 18, 2026 Republican primary with 45.6%, defeating former colleague Kevin Steele (30.2%). He calls himself 'MAGA Mike' and says he has supported Donald Trump since 2015.

candidates.name: Salomon Hernandez Sr.
candidates.occupation: Write-in candidate: the name is not printed on the ballot; voters must write it on the blank line
candidates.background: Salomon Hernandez Sr. is a write-in candidate in Florida's 14th Congressional District. He came to the United States from San Luis Potosi, Mexico, and has lived and worked in Tampa for decades as a landscaper and security consultant. He says he is not a politician and ran at the urging of his grandchildren.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

healthcare.summary: In a television-station candidate questionnaire, Hernandez said his campaign is built on pushing for universal health care for Tampa residents, plus temporary coverage for tourists, citing models he says are used in other tourism economies.
healthcare.quote: Running on pure policy based decisions such as pushing for the city Tampa to provide universal healthcare to residents as well as temporary healthcare to tourists

sources.title: Meet the candidates: Questionnaire for US District 14 (ABC Action News/WFTS, undated; read 2026-09-21)

other_issues.title: Monopolies and unions
other_issues.summary: Hernandez named corporate concentration as the most important issue in the race, saying a "neo union busting mentality is existential," and says he would prioritize small businesses over large corporations to preserve the character of the Tampa Bay area.

sources.title: Meet the candidates: Questionnaire for US District 14 (ABC Action News/WFTS, undated; read 2026-09-21)

candidates.name: Brian Lambert
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.occupation: Retired U.S. Navy (20 years); aircraft mechanic, flight engineer and intelligence specialist
candidates.background: Brian Lambert is the Libertarian candidate in Florida's 14th Congressional District. He served 20 years in the U.S. Navy as an aircraft mechanic, flight engineer and intelligence specialist, including duty at U.S. Central Command in Tampa, and retired in 2018. Since then he has coached Little League, studied culinary arts and is working toward an associate degree in firearms technology. He describes himself as a constitutional libertarian and a father of three.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

taxes.summary: Lambert says Washington has a spending problem rather than a revenue problem and would back reduced spending, a balanced budget and letting people keep more of what they earn.
taxes.quote: Lower taxes. Responsible spending. End government waste.

sources.title: Brian Lambert for Congress campaign website (undated; read 2026-09-21)
Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey: Brian Lambert

veterans.summary: Lambert, a 20-year Navy veteran, says veterans' care should mean greater choice, less bureaucracy and real accountability, with the veteran put first. He frames the issue as reforming delivery of benefits rather than expanding programs.
veterans.quote: greater choice, less bureaucracy, real accountability, and care that puts the veteran first

sources.title: Brian Lambert for Congress campaign website (undated; read 2026-09-21)

guns.summary: Lambert supports nationwide permitless (constitutional) carry for law-abiding adults and national reciprocity, and opposes bans on commonly owned firearms and magazines.
guns.quote: I support constitutional carry nationwide for law-abiding adults. No permit. No government permission slip.

sources.title: Brian Lambert for Congress: Second Amendment (campaign website, undated; read 2026-10-07)

immigration.summary: Lambert supports securing all borders and ports of entry with enforcement, technology, staffing and barriers where practical, consistent enforcement of immigration law and ending incentives for illegal entry, while supporting legal immigration. He does not call for mass deportation.
immigration.quote: I support securing all of America's borders and ports of entry through effective enforcement, modern technology, properly staffed personnel, and physical barriers where they are practical and effective.

sources.title: Brian Lambert for Congress: Border Security & Immigration (campaign website, undated; read 2026-10-07)

education_choice.summary: Lambert says parents should be free to choose public, charter, private, home or career-technical schooling and lists educational choice among his commitments, with less federal involvement. He does not say how public funding should follow students.
education_choice.quote: They deserve the freedom to choose the educational environment that gives their child the greatest opportunity to succeed, whether that's a public school, charter school, private school, homeschool, career and technical education, or another path

sources.title: Brian Lambert for Congress: Education (campaign website, undated; read 2026-10-07)

healthcare.summary: Lambert favors patient choice, price transparency, market competition and fewer federal mandates, saying access does not improve when Washington makes more decisions; he also says the government must keep its health-care promises to veterans.
healthcare.quote: I support expanding patient choice through free-market competition, greater price transparency, and fewer unnecessary federal mandates.

sources.title: Brian Lambert for Congress: Healthcare Reform (campaign website, undated; read 2026-10-07)

energy.summary: Lambert backs an all-of-the-above energy strategy, including oil, gas, nuclear and renewables where economical, driven by free markets rather than government mandates or subsidies.
energy.quote: I support an all-of-the-above energy strategy that allows American producers to compete and innovate in a free market.

sources.title: Brian Lambert for Congress: Energy & American Independence (campaign website, undated; read 2026-10-07)

elections.summary: Lambert says elections should be secure, transparent and easy for eligible citizens to use while making fraud hard to commit, with states continuing to run elections. He neither calls for new restrictions nor for expanded mail voting.
elections.quote: I support election systems that are secure, transparent, and easy for eligible citizens to use while making fraud difficult to commit and easy to detect.

sources.title: Brian Lambert for Congress: Election Integrity (campaign website, undated; read 2026-10-07)

other_issues.title: Constitutional limits on federal power
other_issues.summary: Lambert says every vote he casts would start with whether the measure is constitutional, and that he would work to limit federal power and return responsibilities to the states.

sources.title: Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey: Brian Lambert

candidates.name: Keith Varian
candidates.occupation: Write-in candidate: the name is not printed on the ballot; voters must write it on the blank line
candidates.background: Keith Varian is a write-in candidate in Florida's 14th Congressional District who works in the construction trades and has college coursework in criminal justice and economics. He says he is a political outsider running without party backing and that his priority is the cost of living for District 14 households.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

taxes.summary: Varian says his priority is cutting costs and ending what he calls partisan waste in the federal budget, and during a 2026 fuel-price spike he called for suspending the gas tax and using state reserves for relief at the pump.
taxes.quote: my priority is cutting costs, ending partisan waste, and restoring economic relief directly to District 14 households

sources.title: Meet the candidates: Questionnaire for US District 14 (ABC Action News/WFTS, undated; read 2026-09-21)
Vote Varian 2026 campaign website (undated; read 2026-09-21)

tariffs.summary: In a Ballotpedia candidate survey, Varian described tariffs as a driver of inflation that will add to household costs and the national debt.
tariffs.quote: inflation from tariffs will drown us in a sea of debt

sources.title: Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey: Keith Varian (completed 2025; read 2026-09-21)

social_security.summary: Varian says his goal is keeping Social Security solvent by cutting government waste and raising revenue rather than by reducing benefits for seniors.
social_security.quote: ensuring Social Security remains solvent by identifying and reducing government waste while increasing revenue streams that do not involve cutting benefits for seniors

sources.title: Vote Varian 2026 campaign website (undated; read 2026-09-21)

other_issues.title: Housing costs
other_issues.summary: Varian says home affordability is the biggest issue facing Floridians and that owning a home in the state is getting harder each day, but he does not name specific federal housing policies.

sources.title: Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey: Keith Varian (completed 2025; read 2026-09-21)

other_issues.title: Infrastructure
other_issues.summary: He says roads and power grids should be built to last for generations, arguing durable infrastructure prevents costly breakdowns and utility rate increases.

sources.title: Vote Varian 2026 campaign website (undated; read 2026-09-21)
